title: Elements 1 to 20
note: Atomic number rises by one from each cell to the next. Periods are rows and groups are columns; elements in the same group share similar chemistry because their outer electron arrangements are alike.

items.ex: The lightest element; its most common atom is one proton and one electron.
A noble gas and the second most abundant element in the universe.
The lightest metal, used in rechargeable lithium-ion batteries.
A light, stiff alkaline earth metal used in aerospace parts and X-ray windows.
A metalloid used to make heat-resistant borosilicate glass.
The backbone of organic molecules; diamond and graphite are both pure carbon.
Makes up about 78 percent of Earth’s atmosphere as N₂.
About 21 percent of air and the most abundant element in Earth’s crust by mass.
The most electronegative element.
A noble gas that glows red-orange in discharge signs.
A soft alkali metal that reacts vigorously with water; half of table salt, NaCl.
The metal ion at the center of every chlorophyll molecule.
The most abundant metal in Earth’s crust.
The metalloid at the heart of computer chips; second most abundant element in the crust.
Part of the sugar-phosphate backbone of DNA and of ATP.
A yellow nonmetal found in the amino acids cysteine and methionine.
A yellow-green halogen gas used to disinfect drinking water.
The most abundant noble gas in air, a little under 1 percent.
An alkali metal; K⁺ is the main positive ion inside cells.
An alkaline earth metal and the main mineral element in bones and teeth.

title: Transition metals
note: Groups 3 to 12 hold the transition metals. Period 4 runs from scandium to zinc; below them sit heavier relatives such as silver, platinum, and gold.

items.ex: The first transition metal; small amounts strengthen aluminum alloys.
Strong, light, and corrosion-resistant, so it is used in implants and aircraft.
Added to steel for toughness and used in vanadium redox flow batteries.
Gives stainless steel its corrosion resistance and chrome plating its shine.
Essential in steelmaking; a cluster of manganese atoms splits water in photosynthesis.
The most-used metal; it binds oxygen in the heme groups of hemoglobin.
The metal at the center of vitamin B₁₂.
A magnetic metal used in stainless steel and coins.
An excellent electrical conductor used in most wiring.
A cofactor in many enzymes; coats steel in galvanizing.
Absorbs few neutrons, so it clads nuclear fuel rods.
Hardens steel and sits at the active site of nitrogenase.
A rare platinum-group metal used in catalytic converters.
Can absorb hundreds of times its own volume of hydrogen gas.
Has the highest electrical conductivity of any element.
A toxic metal once common in nickel-cadmium batteries.
Has the highest melting point of any metal, about 3,400 °C.
The densest naturally occurring element.
An iridium-rich clay layer marks the asteroid impact at the end of the Cretaceous.
An unreactive precious metal in catalytic converters and the cancer drug cisplatin.
Very unreactive and the most malleable metal.
The only metal that is liquid at room temperature.

title: Heavier main-group elements
note: Groups 1, 2, and 13 to 18 are the main-group elements. Moving down a group, atoms get larger and more metallic: carbon is a nonmetal, but tin and lead are metals.

items.ex: Melts at about 30 °C, so it can melt in your hand.
A metalloid Mendeleev predicted as eka-silicon; used in early transistors.
A toxic metalloid long infamous as a poison.
A trace element built into antioxidant enzymes as selenocysteine.
The only nonmetal that is liquid at room temperature.
A noble gas whose light defined the meter from 1960 to 1983.
An alkali metal used in compact atomic clocks.
Its salts give fireworks a bright red color.
Indium tin oxide is the transparent conductor coating touchscreens.
Alloyed with copper to make bronze; used to coat steel cans.
A metalloid used in flame retardants and lead-acid battery alloys.
A metalloid used in cadmium telluride solar cells.
A halogen the thyroid needs to make its hormones.
A noble gas that still forms compounds such as XeF₄.
An atomic transition in cesium-133 defines the SI second.
Barium sulfate is swallowed as a contrast agent for X-rays of the gut.
A highly toxic metal once used in rat poison.
A dense, toxic metal and the stable end of uranium and thorium decay chains.
The heavy metal in the stomach remedy bismuth subsalicylate.
A radioactive element discovered by Marie and Pierre Curie and named for Poland.
A radioactive halogen and the rarest naturally occurring element in Earth’s crust.
A radioactive noble gas that can build up in basements.
A highly radioactive alkali metal discovered by Marguerite Perey in 1939.
A radioactive alkaline earth metal discovered by the Curies; once painted on glowing watch dials.

title: Lanthanides, actinides, and other notables
note: The two rows set below the table are the inner transition metals: the lanthanide row follows lanthanum and the actinide row follows actinium. Nearly every element past uranium is made in reactors or accelerators.

items.ex: Part of yttrium barium copper oxide, a high-temperature superconductor.
Niobium-titanium wire forms the superconducting magnets in MRI scanners.
The lightest element with no stable isotope; Tc-99m is a common imaging tracer.
Absorbs neutrons strongly, so it is used in nuclear control rods.
A corrosion-resistant metal used in tiny capacitors in phones.
One of the rarest elements in the crust; used in jet-engine superalloys.
Gives its name to the lanthanide series.
The most abundant lanthanide; cerium oxide polishes glass.
Neodymium-iron-boron magnets are the strongest permanent magnets.
Europium phosphors supply the red in many screens and lamps.
Gadolinium compounds are used as MRI contrast agents.
Gives its name to the actinide series.
A radioactive metal that can breed fissile uranium-233 in reactors.
Fission of uranium-235 powers most nuclear reactors.
The first transuranium element, made in 1940.
Plutonium-238 heat powers generators on deep-space probes.
Americium-241 is the radiation source in many smoke detectors.
Named for Marie and Pierre Curie.
Californium-252 is a strong neutron source.
First found in the debris of the 1952 hydrogen bomb test.
Named for Dmitri Mendeleev, who built the periodic table.
Named for Alfred Nobel.
Element 104, named for Ernest Rutherford.
Element 112, named for Nicolaus Copernicus.
Element 114, named for the Flerov Laboratory in Dubna, Russia.
Element 117, named for the state of Tennessee.
Element 118, the heaviest known; it sits in group 18 under radon.
